derivation: Let R(n) be the existing at-most-F32 Metal capacity bound. safemlx native RoPE retains one output per first-axis batch before concatenating. Each batch adds R(elements/batches), one integer-offset scalar and, with supplied frequencies, R(dimensions/2) for a possible F32 cast. More than one batch additionally adds R(elements) for concatenation.

Metal uses its result buffer for a partial-rotation copy or unsupported strided layout; it does not require a second full internal copy. Output storage can alias the input in the one-batch native case, so metadata retains that input owner while charging the possible allocation.

Constructed scaled operators can flatten leading axes before native application and restore the result shape. Both possible reshape copies are included. Native YaRN additionally prices input amplitude multiplication and possible scalar/input casts.

Explicit input products include input/final reshapes; integer positions and F32 conversion; angle construction; trigonometric, amplitude and dtype buffers; six pair products/sums; interleaving/concatenation, integer-index reshape copies and untouched tails. Native nontraditional wavelength scaling instead includes F32 promotion of the four input-half products.

Wavelength frequency construction has at most 20 half-dimension buffers (including a possible reciprocal) and 16 scalar buffers through its power, comparisons and interpolation graph. Other constructed policies include their host frequency arrays and possible reciprocal. This first-use allowance remains charged on later calls; tighter request composition must separately identify and deduplicate persistent internal frequency state.

Explicit cosine/sine application includes their dtype casts, rotated-half concatenation, both full products and sum, and possible promotion casts. Native signed-integer dispatcher geometry and explicit position endpoints are checked before a bound is returned.

numerical_reference.implementation: independent host f64 frequency-scaling, sine/cosine and paired rotation equation; nonzero binary-fraction inputs; direct supplied frequencies are exact odd integers; explicit embedding products have a separate broadcast-index oracle
numerical_reference.precision_note: Ordinary host equation does not emulate every intermediate F16/BF16 rounding step. Native YaRN scales the whole input including an unrotated tail; InputProducts scales only rotated pairs, matching the existing policies.
